title: A Mechanistic Study of Automated Failure Attribution in LLM-based Agentic Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.28811v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. However, this collaborative structure introduces new challenges for reliably evaluating and diagnosing system failures, particularly failure attribution: tracing a system's execution to identify the agent step responsible for an incorrect final outcome. Because manually performing this task is time- and labor-intensive, recent work has turned to LLMs as judges to automate the process, referred to as automated failure attribution (AFA). These approaches assume that a sufficiently capable model can infer the failing step directly from an interaction transcript. In practice, however, direct prompting often performs poorly, which motivates follow-up work that explores various ways to improve AFA performance, including alternative prompting strategies a

translated_title: 基于大语言模型的智能体系统中自动化失败归因的机制研究
translated_abstract: 智能体系统通过让多个基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体相互协作、并行执行子任务，在复杂任务上展现出了强大的能力。然而，这种协作结构为可靠地评估和诊断系统故障带来了新的挑战，尤其是失败归因问题：即追踪系统的执行过程，以识别导致最终错误结果的责任智能体步骤。由于人工执行这项任务既耗时又费力，近期的研究工作开始转向使用大语言模型作为裁判来自动化这一过程，称为自动化失败归因。这些方法假设一个足够强大的模型能够直接从交互记录中推断出失败的步骤。然而在实践中，直接提示往往表现不佳，这促使后续工作探索各种提升AFA性能的方法，包括替代性提示策略等。
tldr: 本文对基于大语言模型的智能体系统中的自动化失败归因进行了机制层面的研究，分析了为何直接提示方法效果不佳，并探索了提升失败归因性能的改进策略。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a mechanistic study of automated failure attribution (AFA) in LLM-based agentic systems, investigating why direct prompting often performs poorly and exploring strategies to improve failure attribution performance.
